More reasonable would be to make them Read Only from apps, but even then I think that would stop people from participating who could otherwise have taken part in the discussion properly. My best friend was without Internet for his laptop for a few weeks while he moved, and being forced to use your phone is limiting enough without being shut out of your favourite forums. Plus, sometimes short comments make sense. Not every contribution to a discussion is three long paragraphs. Sometimes back and forthing with links is plenty, and you can always have rules for the sub that sets quality standards for comments.

This seems to be a better solution to the problem. As my phone is what I do nearly everything on, being restricted from them completely would be a huge issue. But if discussions were read only on mobile, it would allow people to keep updated with the content without being able to post into them. Mobile discussions could fall apart, but so can normal ones.

This is more of a restriction issue than a content issue. The question asked should be "Do we, as a growing site, decide to block people who want to reach out for our content?"

Because as soon as the answer to that is yes, the freedom of speech won't be able to stand.

I guess read only would be better than to completely block people. Though I still think that discussions are better held on the computer even if a lot of people only use their phones to browse. And of course sometimes short comments do make sense but they can get a response that is much bigger which in turn would have someone who posted that small comment, comment back with a larger comment. Which they can't do properly on a phone.

And moderators will not uphold the quality standards for comments in very long comment chains on threads with lots of comments. Too much to look at for a bunch of mods.
